landscape noun

the look of the land, scenery

also scenery, the lie of the land, beautiful scenery

classical

Tac. Ann. 4.67: faciem locī verteret (Lewis & Short, s.v. faciēs)

faciēs locī

the look of a place, its landscape

Latin speaks of the look (faciēs), the lie (situs) or the loveliness (amoenitās) of a place, or simply of the places (loca), rather than of a landscape. faciēs is first the face, and then any outward form or appearance (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • amoenitās, amoenitātis f. — lovely scenery, the charm of a place

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Q.fr. 3.1.1: summā cum amoenitāte; M-O s.v. scenery

    Loveliness, “in general of objects affecting the sense of sight” (Lewis & Short, s.v. amoenus): of gardens, rivers and coasts. loca amoena (Varro, Sallust) are pleasant places, lovely scenery.

  • regiōnis fōrma — landscape

    also used · modern · Traupman 337

    Traupman’s phrase. regiō is a district or region, fōrma a shape; for a view from a height see view.

  • topia, topiōrum n. pl. — landscape painting

    noun, second declension, plural · also used · classical · Vitr. 7.5.2 (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. forms: landscape

    Only of landscapes painted on walls; a landscape gardener is a topiārius (Cic.; M-O).

Examples

  • cum locīs ipsīs dēlectēmur, montuōsīs etiam et silvestribus, in quibus diūtius commorātī sumus

    since we take pleasure in places themselves, even mountainous and wooded ones, where we have stayed for a long timeCic. Amic. 68

  • ex propinquō vīsa montium altitūdō nivēsque caelō prope immixtae

    the height of the mountains, seen from close by, and the snows almost blending with the skyLiv. 21.32.7

  • in Arpīnātī summā cum amoenitāte, tum salūbritāte flūminis mē refēcī

    at Arpinum I recovered by the river, in the loveliest and healthiest of placesCic. Q.fr. 3.1.1

  • aspectus regiōnis

    the sceneryTraupman 374

See also view, countryside, mountain.
